subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 28, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 28, 2026

Our development team has merged a critical fix for NVIDIA users experiencing no-signal boot issues on live media. The solution adds a KMS hook to the live initramfs configuration, ensuring proper graphics initialization during the boot process. This change has been integrated into the release-1 branch and will be included in the next ISO refresh.

The TU Chemnitz mirror has been officially added to our mirror network after verification against the origin SHA256SUMS. This new mirror expands our European distribution capacity and provides faster download speeds for users in that region. We continue to validate all mirrors to maintain the integrity and security of our distribution channels.

A new backgrounds submodule has been established, tracking the AcreetionOS GitLab repository for wallpaper assets. The initial commit in the acreetionos-wallpapers repository sets the foundation for a curated collection of desktop backgrounds. This modular approach allows us to manage visual assets independently while keeping ISO builds streamlined.

Community security updates from AlmaLinux and Debian have been monitored closely this week, covering packages from kernel and ghostscript to grafana and mariadb. Our team reviews upstream security advisories daily to assess impact on AcreetionOS packages and users. We remain committed to rapid response when vulnerabilities affect our core software stack.

Dave Täht has been awarded the Jonathan B. Postel Service Award by the Internet Society for his contributions to bufferbloat reduction and network performance. This recognition highlights the importance of latency-aware networking in modern infrastructure. We celebrate community members whose work strengthens the broader open-source ecosystem.

The blog deployment pipeline has been updated with a dedicated build configuration for blog.acreetionos.org on GitHub Pages. This improvement separates blog publishing from the main site workflow, enabling faster content iteration. Readers can expect more frequent technical articles and project updates moving forward.

For users testing the release-1 branch, the NVIDIA KMS hook fix should resolve boot display issues on most modern graphics cards. If you encounter any regressions, please report them through our GitLab issue tracker with your hardware details. Testing feedback directly shapes the stability of our upcoming stable release.

The intelligence sync process has been enhanced to automatically aggregate newsletter content, wiki guides, and feed updates into a unified archive.
